incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated error rate for inference-runtime on pool-gpu-west-3. 542 failures in last 5m (5.6% of requests). Primary signal: CUDA illegal memory access + container restarts. Pager routed to #incidents at 2026-03-14 22:19:37 UTC. Thread started.

alicia (oncall): oncall here — seeing ~5% 500s, some OOMs, some `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`. Is this across all models? any customer-facing outages yet?

matt: quick snapshot: most failures come from node gpu-w3-7 (AZ us-west-3b). logs:```
# kubectl -n inference logs runtime-pod-gpu-w3-7 -c inference-runtime --tail=80
[2026-03-14T22:16:42Z] runtime ERROR: kernel: Caught cuda error: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
[2026-03-14T22:16:42Z] runtime ERROR: stacktrace: runtime::kernel::kv_cache.cpp:load_chunk+0x1b2
[2026-03-14T22:16:43Z] kernel: Process killed due to OOM
[2026-03-14T22:17:01Z] containerd: container runtime exited: signal 11
```
Few pods show `SIGSEGV` and then container restarts.

alicia (oncall): thanks. sanjay can you confirm if this matches the pattern from last month (pagewalk/misaligned-address race)?

sanjay: looks suspiciously similar. last time we had concurrent eviction + async DMA leading to misaligned GPU VA in the kernel driver. Differences: previous was single model hotloop; current is mix of short-chat requests + long-context batched generator. Higher prefix cache churn.

matt: also seeing dmesg from gpu-w3-7:```
[  945.123456] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3d:00.0: firmware: load failed
[  945.123458] NVRM: Xid (0001:0000): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  946.223001] kernel: gpu_va: misaligned addr 0x7fffaabbccdd
```
That misaligned addr line is new.

infra-bot: suggested immediate actions: 1) cordon gpu-w3-7 2) drain non-critical inference pods 3) trigger fallback routing to dedicated-capacity-east for impacted customer routes. Shall I run cordon?

alicia (oncall): yes cordon it. infra-bot, please cordon + start drain with --ignore-daemonsets. keep 1 replica of critical routes.

infra-bot: `kubectl cordon gpu-w3-7` executed. Draining non-critical pods now. Will skip critical pods with label critical=true.

support-lead: Heads-up: Customer AcmeCorp reported ~7% of calls failing over the last 10m — they are on hosted API hitting gpt-compat-large on us-west region. I've flagged INC-4821 in zendesk and emailed account exec.

alicia (oncall): good. Matt, can you collect a full core dump and dmesg before we reboot the node? if SIGSEGV repeated, we should dump and upload to S3 for kernel team.

matt: trying to attach. note: some nodes fail to produce coredump because of container runtime restart loop. command I'm running now:```
sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver -b --no-pager > /tmp/gpu-w3-7.dmesg
sudo gcore -o /tmp/core-inference-$(date +%s) $(pidof inference-runtime) || true
aws s3 cp /tmp/gpu-w3-7.dmesg s3://redwood-incident-logs/1765007777/
```
Uploading logs. coredump attempt hit permission error on container runtime. Capturing `/proc/<pid>/maps` instead.

sanjay: capture `pagemap` and `iommu` tables if you can. Also note kernel version on that node is 5.15.104-rt — we've seen a driver regressor on that exact kernel + 525.x driver. Add driver version to log.

matt: driver version `525.116.04`. adding to upload.

alicia (oncall): mitigation checklist update: cordoned node, draining. For immediate traffic: route 25% of traffic on affected model -> dedicated fallback (dedicated-east-2) and add a 200ms incremental backoff retry on client SDK for 503s. deploy-bot, can we set rollback routing?

deploy-bot: Canary route created: `fallback:dedicated-east-2` with weight 25%. Will increase to 50% in 10m if error rate improves.

support-lead: communication plan — sending customers a short note: "We're investigating elevated errors in us-west affecting some generation requests. We have mitigations and are diverting traffic. We'll update in 30m." Anyone object?

alicia (oncall): go ahead. Add note to status.redwood.ai that this is partial degradation for model gpt-compat-large in us-west.

matt: uploaded logs: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1765007777/dmesg.txt and maps.txt. Also pasted a snippet of kernel oops:```
[ 946.223001] kernel BUG at drivers/gpu/gpu_va.c:1023!
[ 946.223003] invalid opcode: 0000 [#1] PREEMPT SMP
[ 946.223010] RIP: 0010:gpu_va_handle_fault+0x6b/0x130 drivers/gpu/gpu_va.c:1023
[ 946.223020] RAX: 0000000000000000 RBX: 00007fffaa11bb22
```
This looks like a kernel-level access to an invalid GPU VA.

sanjay: yep that's a kernel oops point. Next steps: collect VMCore + sosreport, upload, and open a bug with kernel GPU driver team and NV if reproduction holds. Mark priority P0 for driver regressions. I'll draft the bug.

alicia (oncall): are we seeing any correlation with autoscaling events / eviction spikes? maybe large GCs causing huge VM alloc churn.

matt: cluster metrics show a burst of cache eviction and KV cache misses starting ~22:12 UTC coincident with the failure window. Batching rate spiked for gpt-compat-large due to a client replays.

support-lead: customer AcmeCorp traffic pattern: sudden replay of 1000 requests over 30s after a retry bug on their side. We should note that as contributing factor but not root cause.

alicia (oncall): mitigation summary for incident channel: 1) cordoned and drained gpu-w3-7 2) rerouted 25% traffic to dedicated-east-2 3) increased backoff client-side and retried queued requests 4) uploaded logs + kernel dump attempts 5) escalated to kernel/driver team and NV support.

infra-bot: recommended longer-term mitigations: disable async DMA for eviction path on affected kernel, pin runtime to deterministic memmap layout, add preflight for large-burst traffic to limit batch size. Raising infra task INFRA-1279.

sanjay: also recommended: add a safety check in runtime to catch misaligned GPU VA before issuing DMA — return controlled error and fallback instead of hitting kernel. I'll open runtime PR.

matt: I'll reboot node after final log collection. ETA 5m. Reboots should remove immediate instability.

alicia (oncall): keep me posted. If reboots don't stop SIGSEGVs, next step is to cordon entire pool and failover traffic.

(8 minutes later)

matt: node rebooted, pods rescheduled. Early telemetry: error rate dropped to 1.2% and no further SIGSEGVs on new nodes. Canary fallback increased to 50% to validate.

support-lead: customer AcmeCorp updated — errors back down to normal for them. Will confirm with additional observability checks.

alicia (oncall): good progress. owners: sanjay (postmortem + driver bug), matt (logs + node repro artifacts), infra (INFRA-1279). We'll keep this thread open until NV reply. Creating incident INC-1765007777 and linking zendesk INC-4821.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1765007777 created. Severity: Sev2. SLA affected: some tail latency and error rate increased for hosted inference in us-west. Postmortem owner: sanjay. Estimated incident duration: ongoing.

end of thread: ongoing updates will be appended here as we get NV feedback and kernel patch validation."
